newsitem.title: BELARUS: Murderers dismantle wall, escape Belarus prison.
newsitem.headline: Murderers dismantle wall, escape Belarus prison.

text.p: Ten criminals, most of them convicted murderers, dismantled a wall and escaped from prison in the western Belarus city of Brest on Friday morning, a police spokesman said.

Viktor Vasilevsky, a spokesman for Brest police, said an "emergency regime" had been imposed in the city near the Polish frontier and border guards were put on high state of alert along the Polish and Ukrainian frontiers.
"We have some questions to the guard -- it wasn't very attentive. How it can happen that they took down the wall, went into the prison yard and then escaped?," he said.
"Most of those who escaped committed murder and bandit attacks. They were convicted of very heavy crimes," he added.
Vasilevsky said the part of the prison where the escape took place was built in the Soviet era, while the rest dated from between World Wars One and Two when Brest was part of Poland.
"I don't exlude that they will try to get to Poland with false documents," Vasilevsky said of the group, which consisted of seven Belarussians, two Russians and an Armenian.
